- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or neutral, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish or stagnant sentiment.  
- Model consistently underestimates price peaks in the 10–15 day horizon after spikes; adjust upward by 2–5% for such periods.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early 30-day forecasts — overcorrects after sharp moves; apply a smoothing filter or lagged trend correction.  
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5–7 days of the 30d window; apply a “warm-up” correction: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for early days if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33 values (indicating strong bullish sentiment), model tends to lag; increase forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts when sentiment is flat (0.00) — model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day average.
